task.description: Write ExUnit tests satisfying REQ-174's acceptance criteria. Per the design's own SS4 test-design shape: Test A (via ModuleVersionRegistry.invoke/4 or equivalent, in test/letflow/engine/wasm/module_version_registry_test.exs) -- register/activate the req174_memory_write.wat module, invoke write_marker (invocation N), then invoke read_marker (invocation N+1) on the SAME registered/activated module, assert read_marker returns 0 (not 1) -- proving no residue crosses invocations. Test B (via PluginHandler.run_guest/3 or its equivalent call path, in test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs) -- same two-call pattern, independently, since it's a distinct instantiation call site from ModuleVersionRegistry's. Apply this project's mutation-testing discipline where it makes sense (e.g. temporarily make the test use a SHARED store/pid across both calls to confirm the test would actually catch a real isolation violation, then revert -- this is exactly the kind of test whose discriminating power should be proven, not assumed, per this project's history of catching test-design flaws this way). Do not write a new pooling module -- none exists, and the design explicitly declines pooling. Do not modify any production logic in lib/letflow/engine/wasm/. Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test yourself, quote real output.
acceptance_criteria: a test asserts per-invocation isolation regardless of which way the decision went: data written to guest memory in invocation N is NOT observable in invocation N+1 of the same module

the moduledoc states that this requirement restates WASM-13 by ADDING the per-invocation memory-reset correctness constraint, which is absent from WASM-13's original text, and cites decision 0014 (e) and the wasmex Store-reuse behaviour that motivates it
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
